title: SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014: registration and eligibility
objectives: List the registration conditions for an individual and a firm.
State the role of NISM certification and continuing duties.
body_md:
The regulations set who can be an RA and what they must keep doing.

## Individual RA

- Meets the prescribed **educational qualification** and holds a valid **NISM-Series-XV certificate** (or an equivalent recognised qualification).
- Is a fit and proper person, with no disqualifying record.
- Has a place of business and the infrastructure to keep records.

## Firm (research entity)

- Needs the same qualification at the level of its principal officers and analysts.
- Names a **compliance officer** and has written policies on conflicts and trading.
- Registers each analyst as a person responsible for research.

## Continuing duties

| Duty | What it means |
|---|---|
| Pay prescribed fees | On time, to stay registered |
| Keep records | Reports, rationale, client communications, for at least five years |
| Keep certification current | Re-certify before the NISM certificate lapses |
| Cooperate with SEBI | Provide information and accept inspection |

> **Exam tip:** Remember the pairing: qualification plus NISM certification plus fit and proper.
example: A firm hires an analyst whose NISM certificate lapsed last month. Until it is renewed, the analyst should not be responsible for publishing research.
say: My certification is valid until the date on the certificate.
All research and its rationale are kept for at least five years.
never: The certificate is a one-time paper; it never expires.
We delete old drafts to save space.

check.q: Which certification is expected of a research analyst?
check.why: NISM-Series-XV is the research analyst certification.

check.q: Records of research and rationale should be kept for at least:
check.why: The regulations require a minimum five-year record.
A compliance officer oversees conflicts, trading and disclosures.
